extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry/number theory evaluating Mochizuki's IUTT and the Scholze-Stix report
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for assessing the mathematical correctness, completeness, and interpretation of Mochizuki's Inter-Universal Teichmuller Theory (IUTT) and critiques such as the Scholze-Stix report. Focuses on required input data, reconstruction results, role of geometric base-points, and connections to p-adic Hodge theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting a proof must be based on complete understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: If Mochizuki’s proof has to be rejected, then it must be based on a complete understanding of its ideas and present correct mathematical arguments, precisely identifying the issue(s) with its claimed strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques should not rest on superficial readings or assertions; they must isolate the precise mathematical gap(s) with clarity and rigor. The author emphasizes that rejection requires demonstration of errors grounded in full comprehension of the theory's constructions and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify geometric base-point datum for tempered fundamental groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s Key Principle of Inter-Universality requires remembering the geometric base-points for tempered fundamental groups, i.e. one works with Πtemp_{X/E;K} and not Πtemp_{X/E}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any correct exposition or critique must state and use the full geometric base-point datum (a K-valued geometric base-point) rather than omitting it. The comparison table and §1.2.1 stress that tempered fundamental groups depend on the chosen algebraically closed, perfectoid K (and related tilting/untilt data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include algebraically closed perfectoid field and tilting/untilt data (untilts)
rubrics_metrics.description: For important reasons, one works with an algebraically closed perfectoid field K, together with tilting data i.e. one works with untilts rather than K alone; precise datum required (see Joshi, 2022, Definition 5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses must not treat K solely by cardinality or ignore the tilting/untilt structure. The document cautions readers against assuming mere perfectoid-field data is adequate without the untilt/tilting information that Mochizuki's Key Principle invokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits of anabelian reconstruction (cannot reconstruct perfectoid field)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s anabelian reconstruction methods cannot provide reconstruction of the perfectoid field in the geometric base-point datum; e.g., Cp cannot be reconstructed from the topological absolute Galois group G_{Q_p}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments that rely on anabelian reconstruction must account for what theorems actually determine. One cannot assume that group-theoretic reconstructions recover the full geometric base-point information; critiques using reconstruction theorems must be precise about their conclusions and omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate Teichmüller theory with moduli theory; show independence from Absolute Grothendieck Conjecture
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of the Teichmüller Theory of the sort Mochizuki claims is independent of the validity of the Absolute Grothendieck Conjecture for hyperbolic curves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should not infer impossibility of Mochizuki's claims from the Absolute Grothendieck Conjecture; Scholze-Stix allegedly conflated Teichmüller and moduli-theoretic issues. Present the logical independence and justify any claimed implications carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand precisely what reconstruction theorems determine (X/E vs K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Πtemp_{X/E;K}, Mochizuki’s reconstruction theorem determines the isomorphism class of X/E but it does not determine K; however Mochizuki’s Key Principle requires remembering geometric base-points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invoking reconstruction theorems one must state exactly which objects are reconstructed. Misreading their conclusions (e.g., assuming K is recovered) leads to invalid inferences such as those attributed to Scholze-Stix (Remark 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate existence (and non-triviality) of distinct Hodge-Theaters
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of distinct Hodge-Theaters (with a fixed decoration) is a proxy for variation of (p-adic) Hodge structures and distinct Hodge-Theaters arise from distinct geometric and arithmetic data; it is insufficient to assert all Hodge-Theaters are isomorphic in a way that forgets underlying data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid presentation must show how distinct Hodge-Theaters arise and why their distinctions matter (i.e., they are not merely isomorphic when forgetting decorations). The author claims his work supplies these demonstrations; critics should require existence proofs rather than dismissals based on coarse isomorphism statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify unusual definitions/formalism by relating them to established theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Mochizuki’s formalism (e.g., perfect Frobenioids and their realifications) should be explained as proxies for modern p-adic Hodge Theory (at all primes simultaneously) and justified in how they replace missing machinery such as tilting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics must not dismiss 'weird' definitions as purposeless without demonstrating why they fail; conversely, proponents should show how the formalism maps to known constructs (e.g., comparisons with perfectoids, Frobenioids, and Fargues-Fontaine theory) to establish mathematical meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include valuation data, log-Links, Theta-Links, and distinct arithmetic-holomorphic structures in hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Key hypotheses include valuation data, log-Links (Mochizuki’s proxy for Frobenius), Theta-Links (claimed via theory of Frobenioids), and distinct arithmetic-holomorphic structures; these are necessary inputs for the operations and degree computations in Mochizuki's framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparison table (§1.3) and accompanying notes stress that omitting these data (as alleged of Scholze-Stix) leads to incorrect mathematical conclusions. Any evaluation must state whether these objects are present or ignored and explain their roles in computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit key mathematical assumptions and aspects when critiquing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports or critiques that omit most key mathematical assumptions and aspects of Mochizuki’s Theory (e.g., geometric base-points, valuation data) produce incorrect conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a critique, list and check all hypotheses the original theory uses. Omitting required inputs (even if tacit) invalidates many derived claims; the author asserts Scholze-Stix and Scholze (2021) made such omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate existence and deformation properties via arbitrary algebraically closed perfectoid fields
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy Mochizuki’s requirements one should demonstrate existence and deformation properties via arbitrary algebraically closed perfectoid fields or equivalently by using arbitrary geometric base-points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete constructions showing existence and deformation (local and global) validate claims about variation and inter-universality. The author cites his own work as providing these demonstrations; evaluators should demand such constructions rather than accept abstract assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctly identify domains and codomains of operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorrect identification of domains and codomains for key operations (e.g., forgetting geometric base-point data) leads to false conclusions about the theory; Scholze-Stix allegedly misidentified such domains/codomains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully trace each operation's input and output objects and ensure any identifications do not implicitly forget essential decorations or base-point data. The comparison table highlights this as a source of error in prior critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain fairness, professional conduct, and mathematical engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Critiques and defenses should be fair and professional; parties should engage in mathematical conversations and address the work of others rather than resorting to dismissals, name-calling or refusing to acknowledge relevant clarifying work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author stresses he has tried to be fair and notes unprofessional behavior (e.g., name-calling) and reticence to acknowledge clarifying work as problematic. Good scholarly practice includes responding to concrete mathematical points and publicly engaging with relevant corrections and clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat conclusions about major conjectures (e.g., abc) as independent of unresolved expository issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclusion of this report is independent of the proof of the abc-conjecture; assessments about whether abc is proved should wait for full verification independent of contested expository or hypothesis-omission issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should separate (a) whether the framework is correctly and fully presented and (b) whether the framework actually proves conjectures. The author maintains neutrality on whether the abc-conjecture has been proved until outstanding issues are tied up.
